{{Short description|English mathematician  (c. 1625–1675)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=May 2022}}
{{Use British English|date=February 2013}}

'''Ralph Greatorex''' (c. 1625–1675)<ref name="ODNB">Sarah Bendall, 'Greatorex, Ralph (c.1625–1675)', Oxford Dictionary of National Biography, Oxford University Press, 2004; online edn, Jan 2008 [http://www.oxforddnb.com/view/article/11365, retrieved 6 Feb 2011]</ref> was an English mathematician, mathematical instrument maker, and an apprentice of London clockmaker [[Elias Allen]].<ref name="ODNB"/>

Greatorex is mentioned in [[John Aubrey]]'s [[Brief Lives]] as a great friend of [[William Oughtred]] the mathematician.<ref name="DNB 1900">[[s:Greatorex, Ralph (DNB00)|Greatorex, Ralph]], Lydia Miller Middleton, Dictionary of National Biography, 1885-1900, Volume 23</ref> He is also briefly referred to in Aubrey's 'Natural History of Wilts', and in the 'Macclesfield Correspondence'.<ref name="DNB 1900"/> [[John Evelyn]] met Greatorex on 8 May 1656, and saw his 'excellent invention to quench fire.'<ref name="DNB 1900"/> His name appears in '[[Pepys's Diary]].'<ref name="DNB 1900"/> On 10 October 1660, when several engines were shown at work in [[St. James's Park]], 'above all the rest,' says [[Samuel Pepys]], 'I liked that which Mr. Greatorex brought, which do carry up the water with a great deal of ease.'<ref name="DNB 1900"/>

On 24 October Pepys bought of Greatorex a drawing-pen, 'and he did show me the manner of the lamp-glasses which carry the light a great way, good to read in bed by, and I intend to have one of them. And we looked at his wooden jack in his chimney, that goes with the smoake, which indeed is very pretty.'<ref name="DNB 1900"/> On 9 June and 20 September 1662 and 23 March 1663 ('this day Greatorex brought me a very pretty weather-glasse for heat and cold') Pepys met the inventor; the last entry, 23 May 1663, refers to his varnish, 'which appears every whit as good upon a stick which he hath done, as the Indian.'<ref name="DNB 1900"/>

As well as Pepys, Allen, Oughtred and Evelyn, others that Greatorex worked or corresponded with included [[Samuel Hartlib]], [[Christopher Wren]], [[Robert Boyle]], [[Edward Phillips]] and [[Jonas Moore]].<ref name="ODNB"/> He also attended meetings of the [[Royal Society]], and did horticultural experiments at [[Arundel House]].<ref name="ODNB"/>
